quotes.text: In the midst of chaos, there is also opportunity.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.source: The Art of War (c. 5th century BC)
quotes.notes: Translated from classical Chinese. Various English translations exist; this phrasing is widely attributed.

quotes.text: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.notes: From the Gregory Hays translation (Modern Library, 2002). Public domain source text.

quotes.text: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.notes: Paraphrased from Meditations. The exact wording varies by translation.

quotes.text: There is nothing outside of yourself that can ever enable you to get better, stronger, richer, quicker, or smarter. Everything is within.
quotes.author: Miyamoto Musashi
quotes.notes: From Go Rin No Sho. Translation varies; this phrasing is from the William Scott Wilson translation.

quotes.text: Do nothing that is of no use.
quotes.author: Miyamoto Musashi
quotes.notes: A widely cited maxim from Go Rin No Sho.

quotes.text: It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Discourses (c. 108 AD), as recorded by Arrian
quotes.notes: Paraphrased from the Discourses. The sentiment is central to Stoic philosophy.

quotes.text: No man is free who is not master of himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.notes: Widely attributed. Found in various compilations of Epictetus's teachings.

quotes.text: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.notes: From 'Maxims and Arrows', section 12. Public domain.

quotes.text: Without music, life would be a mistake.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.notes: From 'Maxims and Arrows', section 33. Public domain.

quotes.text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.source: Tao Te Ching, Chapter 64 (c. 4th century BC)
quotes.notes: Translated from classical Chinese. One of the most widely quoted passages from the Tao Te Ching.

quotes.text: Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.source: Tao Te Ching, Chapter 33 (c. 4th century BC)
quotes.notes: Commonly translated passage. Exact wording varies across translations.

quotes.text: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood. Now is the time to understand more, so that we may fear less.
quotes.author: Marie Curie
quotes.source: Attributed, widely cited in biographical works
quotes.notes: Widely attributed to Curie. Exact original source is debated but the attribution is well established.

quotes.text: I would rather have questions that can't be answered than answers that can't be questioned.
quotes.author: Richard Feynman
quotes.source: Attributed, from various lectures and interviews
quotes.notes: Widely attributed to Feynman. Consistent with his well-documented views on scientific inquiry.

quotes.text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
quotes.author: Richard Feynman
quotes.source: Cargo Cult Science, Caltech commencement address (1974)
quotes.notes: From the published text of his 1974 Caltech commencement address.

quotes.text: Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.
quotes.author: Carl Sagan
quotes.notes: Very commonly attributed to Sagan but the original source is uncertain. May be a paraphrase by a journalist.

quotes.text: For small creatures such as we the vastness is bearable only through love.
quotes.author: Carl Sagan
quotes.notes: From the novel Contact. Copyright considerations: quoted under fair use as a brief excerpt.

quotes.text: Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.notes: Very widely attributed to Wilde but no reliable primary source has been identified.

quotes.text: To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.source: The Soul of Man Under Socialism (1891)
quotes.notes: From the published essay. Public domain.

quotes.text: The secret of getting ahead is getting started.
quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.notes: Commonly attributed to Twain but original source is uncertain.

quotes.text: Whenever you find yourself on the side of the majority, it is time to pause and reflect.
quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.notes: From his published notebooks. Public domain.

quotes.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.notes: Paraphrased from Epistulae Morales. Public domain.

quotes.text: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Attributed, based on Letters to Lucilius
quotes.notes: Widely attributed to Seneca but the exact phrasing is not found in surviving texts.

quotes.text: Imagination is more important than knowledge. Knowledge is limited. Imagination encircles the world.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.source: Interview in The Saturday Evening Post (October 26, 1929)
quotes.notes: From the George Sylvester Viereck interview. Public domain.

quotes.text: Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom.
quotes.author: Aristotle
quotes.source: Attributed, widely cited in philosophical compilations
quotes.notes: Commonly attributed to Aristotle but no specific original source in his surviving works has been confirmed.

quotes.text: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.notes: Widely attributed to Confucius but the exact source in the Analects is uncertain.

quotes.text: Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.
quotes.author: Leonardo da Vinci
quotes.notes: Very commonly attributed to da Vinci. Exact original source is debated.

quotes.text: Go confidently in the direction of your dreams. Live the life you have imagined.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.notes: Paraphrased from the conclusion of Walden. The original text is more verbose. Public domain.

quotes.text: When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
quotes.author: Viktor Frankl
quotes.notes: From the widely published memoir. Brief quotation under fair use.

quotes.text: The world breaks everyone, and afterward, many are strong at the broken places.
quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.notes: From Chapter 34. Published 1929; copyright may still apply in some jurisdictions. Brief quotation under fair use.

quotes.text: The wound is the place where the Light enters you.
quotes.author: Rumi
quotes.notes: Widely attributed to Rumi via Coleman Barks's poetic interpretations. Exact correspondence to Persian original is uncertain.
